title.zh: 史前时期：中华文明的起源

clips.send: In Yuanmou, Yunnan, scientists found early humans from about 1.7 million years ago: Yuanmou Man, the earliest early humans so far confirmed in China.
clips.text: In Yuanmou, Yunnan, scientists found early humans from about 1.7 million years ago: Yuanmou Man, the earliest early humans so far confirmed in China.

clips.send: This is a schematic map of China. Let’s find where early humans and early farming villages were found, and when they lived.
clips.text: This is a schematic map of China. Let’s find where early humans and early farming villages were found, and when they lived.

clips.send: Banpo roof and posts. Wooden posts hold up a roof of branches, grass and mud. Wooden posts stand in the pit and hold up a cone-shaped roof. The roof was covered with branches, thatch and mud to keep out wind and rain. Banpo houses came in round and square shapes.
clips.text: Banpo roof & posts。 Wooden posts hold up a roof of branches, grass and mud。 Wooden posts stand in the pit and hold up a cone-shaped roof.。 The roof was covered with branches, thatch and mud to keep out wind and rain.。 Banpo houses came in round and square shapes.

clips.send: Thatched gable roof and walls. Steep roof sheds the heavy rain. A two-sided (gable) thatched roof lets rain run off quickly. Walls were made of wood and woven reeds, keeping the house light and airy. People lived upstairs; the space under the floor stayed open.
clips.text: Thatched gable roof & walls。 Steep roof sheds the heavy rain。 A two-sided (gable) thatched roof lets rain run off quickly.。 Walls were made of wood and woven reeds, keeping the house light and airy.。 People lived upstairs; the space under the floor stayed open.

clips.send: About 4,000–5,000 years ago, the Yan and Yellow Emperor tribes of the Yellow River valley allied, defeated Chiyou at Zhuolu, and gradually formed the Huaxia people. The two are honoured as the first ancestors of Chinese civilization.
clips.text: About 4,000–5,000 years ago, the Yan and Yellow Emperor tribes of the Yellow River valley allied, defeated Chiyou at Zhuolu, and gradually formed the Huaxia people. The two are honoured as the first ancestors of Chinese civilization.

clips.send: Banpo. Today: Xi’an, Shaanxi. Banpo villagers grew millet, lived in half-underground houses and made painted pottery, like the famous basin with a human face and fish.
clips.text: Banpo. Today: Xi’an, Shaanxi. Banpo villagers grew millet, lived in half-underground houses and made painted pottery, like the famous basin with a human face and fish.

clips.send: At Zhoukoudian near Beijing lived Peking Man, about 700,000–200,000 years ago. They made chipped stone tools, used natural fire and lived in groups.
clips.text: At Zhoukoudian near Beijing lived Peking Man, about 700,000–200,000 years ago. They made chipped stone tools, used natural fire and lived in groups.

clips.send: Put them on a timeline. It uses a log scale: each tick is ten times closer to today. People have lived in China for more than a million years!
clips.text: Put them on a timeline. It uses a log scale: each tick is ten times closer to today. People have lived in China for more than a million years!

clips.send: Sloping doorway. Steps lead down into the sunken room. Because the floor is below ground, a sloping passage with steps leads down into the house. A small shelter over the doorway kept rain out.
clips.text: Sloping doorway。 Steps lead down into the sunken room。 Because the floor is below ground, a sloping passage with steps leads down into the house.。 A small shelter over the doorway kept rain out.

clips.send: Hemudu stilt house. Raised on wooden piles above wet ground. The Hemudu site is in Yuyao, Zhejiang, in the Yangtze River valley, about 7,000 years old. Wooden piles were driven into the ground, beams and floorboards laid on top, then the house built above: a stilt (ganlan-style) house. The south is warm, wet and rainy. A raised floor stays dry, lets air flow, and keeps out snakes and insects.

A raised floor stays dry, lets air flow, and keeps out snakes and insects.

clips.send: Bone spade (si). A farming tool for turning soil (enlarged). A si is a spade made from the shoulder blade of a large animal, tied to a wooden handle. It was used to turn the soil of the rice fields. Hemudu people also used polished stone tools, made black pottery and raised pigs, dogs and water buffalo.

clips.send: Zoom in on the last few thousand years: Hemudu, Banpo, the legendary age of the Yan and Yellow Emperors, then Yao, Shun and Yu, about 2070 BCE, Yu founds the Xia dynasty.
clips.text: Zoom in on the last few thousand years: Hemudu → Banpo → the legendary age of the Yan and Yellow Emperors, then Yao, Shun and Yu → about 2070 BCE, Yu founds the Xia dynasty.

clips.send: Millet field. A drought-tolerant crop for the dry north. Banpo people grew millet (粟, foxtail millet). China is one of the first countries in the world to grow millet. They farmed with polished stone tools such as stone axes, spades and knives, grew vegetables and raised pigs and dogs.

clips.send: Under Yao, Shun and Yu, the tribal alliance chose its leader by abdication: the worthiest, most able person was recommended. Yu tamed the floods and was chosen. Later Yu founded the Xia, and his son Qi inherited the throne.
clips.text: Under Yao, Shun and Yu, the tribal alliance chose its leader by abdication: the worthiest, most able person was recommended. Yu tamed the floods and was chosen. Later Yu founded the Xia, and his son Qi inherited the throne.

clips.send: Rice paddy. A water-loving crop for the wet south. Large amounts of rice grains and husks were found at Hemudu: the people grew rice. China is one of the first countries in the world to grow rice. Rice needs plenty of water, so it suits the warm, wet Yangtze valley.

clips.send: Yellow River. It picks up yellow loess on the plateau and carries it to the Bohai. Early Chinese civilisation grew up along its middle and lower reaches.
clips.text: Yellow River. It picks up yellow loess on the plateau and carries it to the Bohai. Early Chinese civilisation grew up along its middle and lower reaches.

clips.send: Hemudu. Today: Yuyao, Zhejiang. About 7,000 years ago people here grew rice, lived in stilt houses and already joined timbers with mortise-and-tenon joints.
clips.text: Hemudu. Today: Yuyao, Zhejiang. About 7,000 years ago people here grew rice, lived in stilt houses and already joined timbers with mortise-and-tenon joints.

clips.send: Yuanmou. Two front teeth found here in 1965 belong to Yuanmou Man, who lived about 1.7 million years ago — the earliest ancient human yet confirmed in China.
clips.text: Yuanmou. Two front teeth found here in 1965 belong to Yuanmou Man, who lived about 1.7 million years ago — the earliest ancient human yet confirmed in China.

clips.send: In a cave at the top of the same hill lived Upper Cave Man, about 30,000 years ago. They looked like modern people and sewed clothes with bone needles.
clips.text: In a cave at the top of the same hill lived Upper Cave Man, about 30,000 years ago. They looked like modern people and sewed clothes with bone needles.

clips.send: Farming began about 10,000 years ago. Along the Yangtze, Hemudu people grew RICE (about 7,000 years ago); along the Yellow River, Banpo people grew MILLET (about 6,000 years ago).
clips.text: Farming began about 10,000 years ago. Along the Yangtze, Hemudu people grew RICE (about 7,000 years ago); along the Yellow River, Banpo people grew MILLET (about 6,000 years ago).

clips.send: Yangtze River. From the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau to the East China Sea at Shanghai. It is a “golden waterway” full of ships.
clips.text: Yangtze River. From the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau to the East China Sea at Shanghai. It is a “golden waterway” full of ships.

clips.send: Xi’an. Thirteen dynasties had their capital here. In the Xi’an Incident of December 1936, Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng forced Chiang Kai-shek to stop the civil war and fight Japan.
clips.text: Xi’an. Thirteen dynasties had their capital here. In the Xi’an Incident of December 1936, Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng forced Chiang Kai-shek to stop the civil war and fight Japan.

clips.send: 河姆渡。今天：浙江余姚。约7000年前，河姆渡人在这里种植水稻，住干栏式房屋，木构件上已经使用榫卯。

clips.send: 北京周口店龙骨山，生活着距今约 70 万—20 万年的北京人。他们会打制石器，会使用天然火，过着群居生活。

clips.send: 北京。北京是我国的首都，全国的政治中心、文化中心。城市中心的故宫是明清两代的皇宫。

clips.send: 大约一万年前起，人们开始种植作物、定居生活。长江流域的河姆渡人种植水稻（约 7000 年前）；黄河流域的半坡人种植粟（约 6000 年前）。

clips.send: 长江。长江从青藏高原流到上海注入东海，是一条繁忙的“黄金水道”。

clips.send: 半坡：圆锥形屋顶与木柱。 木柱撑起用树枝、茅草和泥土盖成的屋顶。 木柱立在坑里，支撑起圆锥形的屋顶。。 屋顶用树枝、茅草和泥土覆盖，用来挡风遮雨。。 半坡人的房屋有圆形和方形两种。

clips.send: 周口店。今天：北京房山。龙骨山的洞穴里生活过会用火的北京人，后来又有会用骨针缝衣服的山顶洞人。这里已被列入《世界遗产名录》。

clips.send: 半坡：半地穴式房基。 房屋地面向下挖，冬暖、挡风。 半坡遗址位于陕西西安附近，地处黄河流域，距今约 6000 年。。 房屋地面挖到地表以下，一半在地下、一半在地上，叫“半地穴式房屋”。。 北方气候较干燥寒冷，黄土层深厚，向下挖坑既省材料又能保暖挡风。

clips.send: 西安。先后有十三个王朝在这里建都。1936年12月，张学良、杨虎城在这里发动西安事变，逼蒋抗日。

clips.send: 河姆渡：干栏式房屋。 用木桩把房子架离潮湿的地面。 河姆渡遗址位于浙江余姚，地处长江流域，距今约 7000 年。。 先在地上打下木桩，架上横梁、铺上地板，再在上面盖房子——这就是“干栏式房屋”。。 南方温暖湿润、雨水多，房屋架空可以防潮、通风，还能防虫蛇野兽。

clips.send: 河姆渡：水稻。 喜水的南方作物。 河姆渡遗址出土了大量稻谷、稻壳，说明河姆渡人种植水稻。。 我国是世界上最早种植水稻的国家之一。。 水稻需要大量的水，适合温暖湿润的长江流域。
clips.text: 河姆渡：水稻。 喜水的南方作物。 河姆渡遗址出土了大量稻谷、稻壳，说明河姆渡人种植水稻。。 我国是世界上最早种植水稻的国家之一。。 水稻需要大量的水，适合温暖湿润的长江流域。

clips.send: 河姆渡：榫卯结构。 不用钉子就能把木头接牢。 河姆渡遗址发现了带有榫卯的木构件。。 一凸（榫）一凹（卯）相互咬合，把木头牢牢连在一起。。 榫卯成为我国传统木结构建筑的重要技术，一直沿用至今。

clips.send: 半坡。今天：陕西西安。半坡人种植粟，住半地穴式房屋，会制作彩陶，著名的人面鱼纹彩陶盆就出土在这里。

clips.send: 传说距今约四五千年，黄河流域的炎帝部落和黄帝部落结成联盟，在涿鹿打败了蚩尤，逐渐形成了华夏族。炎帝和黄帝被尊为中华民族的“人文初祖”，中华儿女自称“炎黄子孙”。

clips.send: 在云南元谋，发现了距今约 170 万年的古人类——元谋人。他们是我国境内目前已确认的最早的古人类。

clips.send: 半坡：粟（小米）。 耐旱的北方作物。 半坡人种植粟（小米）。。 我国是世界上最早种植粟的国家之一。。 他们使用磨制石器（石斧、石铲、石刀等）耕作，还种植蔬菜，饲养猪、狗等家畜。
